topic.name: The Average of the Roots Formula

question.text: The graph above shows a parabola. The $x$-coordinates of $A$ and $B$ are $\dfrac{11}{6}$ and $\dfrac{25}{6},$ respectively. Find the axis of symmetry of the parabola.
question.explanation:
We're given that the roots of the parabola are $x_1=\dfrac{11}{6}$ and $x_2=\dfrac{25}{6}.$

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

\begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{11}{6}+\dfrac{25}{6}\right)}{2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{36}{6}\right)}{2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{6}{2}\\[5pt] &=3. \end{align*}

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x= 3.$

example.title: Finding the Axis of Symmetry From the X-Intercepts

question.text: Find the axis of symmetry for the parabola $y=-(x-5)(x+7).$
question.explanation:
From the equation $y=-(x-5)(x+7),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-7.$

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

\begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5+(-7)}{2} \\[5pt] &= -1. \end{align*}

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-1.$

example.title: Finding the Axis of Symmetry From the Parabola’s Equation in Factored Form

question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(x-1)(x-9)$ is $x=$
question.explanation:
From the equation $y=(x-1)(x-9),$ we can tell that the roots of the parabola are $x_1=1$ and $x_2=9.$

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

\begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1+9}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{10}{2}\\[5pt] &= 5 \end{align*}

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}.$
